recipes.name: Creamy Bow-Tie Pasta with Chicken and Broccoli
ingredients_raw: 3 tablespoons KRAFT Signature Roasted Red Pepper with Parmesan Dressing
0.5 (250 g) package Philadelphia Light Brick Cream Cheese, cubed

steps.text: Cook pasta as directed on package, adding broccoli to the cooking water for the last 3 min. of the pasta cooking time. Meanwhile, heat dressing in large nonstick skillet on medium heat. Add chicken and garlic; cook 5 min. Turn chicken over; continue cooking 4 to 5 min. or until chicken is cooked through (170 degrees F).

Drain pasta mixture in colander; return to pan and set aside. Add pasta sauce and cream cheese to chicken in skillet; cook on medium-low heat 2 to 3 min. or until cream cheese is completely melted, mixture is well blended and chicken is coated with sauce, stirring occasionally. Remove chicken from skillet; keep warm. Add sauce mixture to pasta mixture; mix well. Transfer to six serving bowls.
Cut chicken crosswise into thick slices; fan out chicken over pasta mixture in each bowl. Sprinkle evenly with Parmesan cheese.

raw_recipe.headline: Creamy Bow-Tie Pasta with Chicken and Broccoli
raw_recipe.description: Chicken breasts cooked in a creamy tomato sauce with bow-tie pasta and broccoli florets make a quick and delicious one-dish dinner.

review.reviewBody: Very Good!! My husband aked if it could be a regular dish, i couldn't find the roasted red pepper dressing so i used the sundried tomato and it was delish!!!!

Yumm! Very good base recipe ... even better with some tweaks! I Cut the chicken into pieces and marinated it overnight in Italian dressing (I couldn't find the Red Pepper kind). Instead of plain cream cheese I used the new Philly Italian Cheese and Herb Cooking Creme which was very flavorful. I also added some chopped red onion and julienned red pepper & carrots in addition to the broccoli. I steamed the broccoli rather than boiled it and then added all the veggies to the chicken/sauce mixture in the skillet. Finally, to add some heat, I tossed in some red pepper flakes. Super easy & fast too which is always a plus.

My family loved this! The only changes I made were to reduce the pasta to 3 cups and increased the broccoli to 5 cups and used non fat cream cheese. Made it lower calorie for us. Really good, easy and quick. Will make often. Thanks!

This was a great recipe! Very easy! I did not have any of the Kraft Dressing so I just grilled the chicken in Olive oil and spices including the garlic. I did a short cut AND a money saving by stiring in a bag of nuked broccoli when it was time to stir all items.

This was a great one! I followed the recipe as best as I could. However, I doubled the garlic, used basil and garlic sauce instead of tomato-basil, and cut the chicken into bite size pieces to saute in the dressing (it went faster). I will definitely be making this again! Thanks!

Excellent and easy dish to make -- I only had 3 chicken breasts left in my bulk package but I left the rest of the recipe the same and just cut them into smaller chunks. Cooked the broccoli a little too long, so definitely keep an eye on that! My chicken breasts were Italian/herb flavored, so I skipped the dressing altogether, and I think it achieved the desired affect.

I didn't have bow tie pasta, so used linguini. I had three chicken breasts were marinated in italian seasonings, and two plain, so just added italian dressing (I'd forgotten to heat the dressing first). The family loved it! Filling, tasty and easy to make = a winner

I used Caesar dressing instead of the roasted red pepper and Parmesan (it's what I had on hand). I also didn't have any pasta sauce so I used a can of tomato sauce and a can of Italian style diced tomatoes. It was tasty! My family devoured it! Will definitely make again.

Absolutely Delish! My small changes...sun dried tomato salad dressing, used an 8 oz. block of regular cream cheese, shredded parmesan. I LoOve pasta, and this one was SO simple for such AMAZING taste! Thanx =)
Kept to the recipe. My husband said he liked it a lot and asked if there was any leftovers the next night, which is saying a lot.

Easy recipe, but way too salty even using less than the recipe called for, and reduced sodium, soy sauce. We couldnt get past the salty. Making the sauce with chicken stock instead of soy sauce and saving the soy sauce as a condiment, may be a better alternative. Next time I would also use more ginger and a little garlic.

Yum!! I'm a mother of 4 and 1 is such a picky eater BUT he loved this!! All the other kids, including my husband, loved it!! I made it exactly as the recipe calls for and it was a hit!! Plenty of flavor!! This is going in the rotation!!
I thought this recipe was just ok. I had higher hopes for it. It turned out a bit on the bland side. I might make again, but I will be adding to this dish to turn it into something spectacular.
Really Good! Super Easy! The whole fam. liked it even the kids! It was a hit in my house!
It was quick, easy and tasted great!

This was just okay. The color of the sauce turned out to be dark orange and it was not appetizing looking and it wasn't the greatest tasting. If I was to make again, and not sure that I would, I would go very light with the pasta sauce, so as to try to keep a lighter color.
